sam: Heads-up — after last night's deploy I see a ~27% drop in prompt-cache hit-rate and p95 latency climbed. Looks correlated to tool/function call metadata changes.
maria: ugh, good catch. do you have numbers/trace? :eyes:
sam: quick snapshot from perf job (canary traffic vs baseline):
```
baseline: hit-rate=81.7%  p50=23ms  p95=110ms  tokens/s=1900
canary:   hit-rate=54.3%  p50=40ms  p95=190ms  tokens/s=1200
```
probable root: we started serializing function/tool `fields` as-is (JS object iteration order), previously they were canonicalized in the producer. order changed for many requests -> different cache keys.
kai: oh interesting — so this is purely key churn, not model change? any kernel-selection fallout? 
sam: mostly key churn, but secondary effects: more unique prefixes -> smaller batch coalescing -> suboptimal kernel paths for several long-seq workloads. saw more kernel-switches in traces.
isha: can you paste an example of the before/after cache key? that helps triage.
sam: sure. example (simplified):
```
// old canonicalized key payload
{"model":"redwood-v1","tokenizer":"tk-v2","system_hash":"s123","tool":{"name":"lookup","fields":[{"k":"id","v":"123"},{"k":"lang","v":"en"}]},"user":"hello"}

// new non-deterministic serialization (order flipped)
{"model":"redwood-v1","tokenizer":"tk-v2","system_hash":"s123","tool":{"name":"lookup","fields":[{"k":"lang","v":"en"},{"k":"id","v":"123"}]},"user":"hello"}
```
These produce different cache keys even though semantically same.
maria: that explains the hit-rate. did the deploy touch any protobuf/serialization lib? alex rolled something? :thinking_face:
alex: I changed the tool metadata producer to stop sorting for perf reasons (avoid extra allocs). I thought the downstream cache keying normalized, but apparently not.
isha: ok two parts: 1) immediate rollback vs mitigation, 2) longer-term keying contract. what's safer short-term?
sam: mitigation: reintroduce canonicalization at cache-key layer (cheap) + pin tokenizer/model/version into the key explicitly. add rule to drop ephemeral fields (e.g., `request_id`, `ts`). previous canonicalization code was ~80us per key; should be acceptable vs p95 delta.
kai: are there any tests guarding this? we need a unit/regression to catch non-deterministic ordering.
alex: will revert my producer change in canary while we add a canonicalizer. also can add a feature-flag to toggle strict canonicalization.
perf-bot: perf.alert: canary job 2103456789 reported regression: cache_hit_rate_drop=27.4% (p<0.01). see: https://perf.internal/runs/2103456789
maria: for the cache-key contract we should define exact fields used: `model`, `model_version`, `tokenizer_version`, `system_prompt_hash`, `canonicalized_user_prompt`, `tool_signature` (sorted keys + values), and `tool_extra` only if `consider_in_key=true`.
isha: +1. also add a checksum for the tool schema: hash(sorted((k,v) pairs)) so we don't leak large tool payloads into keys.
sam: example canonicalization snippet i'll push to PR:
```python
# pseudo
def canonicalize_tool(tool):
    fields = sorted((f['k'], f.get('v','')) for f in tool.get('fields',[]))
    return json.dumps({'name':tool['name'],'fields':fields}, separators=(',',':'))

def compute_cache_key(req):
    parts = [req.model, req.model_version, req.tokenizer_version, hash(req.system_prompt)]
    parts.append(canonicalize_tool(req.tool))
    parts.append(normalize_text(req.user_prompt))
    return sha256(':'.join(parts))
```
alex: that works. i'll open a PR for canary revert + cache-key canonicalizer. can we measure canonicalizer cost? maybe benchmark 1M keys locally.
kai: also add a metric for "cache-key-uniques-per-minute" and track variance. if that spikes after deploy we auto-block.
isha: and add a test that serializes tool object 1000 ways and asserts key stable.
maria: rollout plan: 1) revert producer change in canary (immediate) 2) add canonicalizer + perf test in branch 3) run canary for 12h monitor hit-rate/kernel-switches 4) ship to prod if stable.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: revert-producer-canary -> staging -> canary. ETA 15m.
sam: thanks everyone. i'll collect traces for the windows with highest kernel-switch count and attach to the PR. closing loop once canary proves green. :thumbsup:
